$doc: Fog and the far clip.
RENDER_DIST is how far the ground is seen, in world `u`: where fog
finishes hiding it, with the camera 4,096u from its pivot or nearer;
further out, it and every distance here grow with the camera's
(FOG_PER_DIST). It is as far as the window reaches with its base at the
leaves, which a street-level view holds for its decoration: five levels
put the top at level 4, which draws step 2^5, wanted out to 192 · 2^5 =
6,144u (terrain/level.rs's level_at). The haze in front of it is the
air's (look/atmosphere.rs, aerial perspective), so the fog is only the
edge, and a coarser ring past it costs a ring of pages and not memory:
the window's records are placed at boot. Where ground geometry exists is
no longer a distance
chosen beside it but the page pyramid's: a ring of pages at every level
of a window, drawn to the window's top level's ring (terrain/level.rs,
terrain/config.json), which at the finest window reaches 8192u. Fog
therefore hides ground that is there rather than the edge of where it
stops.
Anchoring the rings at the view centre rather than the camera is what
keeps residency invariant under rotation: at a wide zoom the camera sits
its whole distance from that centre, and following it would sweep pages
in and out on a spin. Which chunk is drawn at which level, and which tier
it shows, are camera-relative — both measure against the camera — so
ground standing above the terrain is ranked where it actually is. Over
every zoom, tilt, aspect ratio and pivot height the camera allows, the
ground in view lies inside what the window's top ring draws
(world/chunk/view_range.test.rs).
VIEW_DIST * 1.5. VIEW_DIST (camera/config.json) is sized past
where the ground is seen, so FAR_CLIP keeps margin over it rather than
being an arbitrary multiple. The fade is FOG_NEAR/FOG_FAR (a smoothstep
in shade.wgsl), and it is total well inside where the ground is drawn,
so ground always fades out instead of being cut off while still visible:
into the sky's own light along the same ray, which the sky pass draws
past it (atmos_view.wgsl), so the edge is not a seam. The haze nearer in
is the air's (aerial perspective), not this band's.
RENDER_DIST * 0.75. The fade starts here and is total at RENDER_DIST, a
distance the ground is drawn past, so it completes instead of being
cut. Narrow, because it only hides where the ground ends: the depth in
front of it is the air's haze.
RENDER_DIST.
Fog's far edge per unit of the camera's distance from its pivot, where
that is the further: FOG_FAR over the 1,024u the camera could stand at
when these were first tuned, kept as the fog was pushed out to the window.
Past the distance where it overtakes FOG_FAR, 4,096u, the fade
and the clip planes grow in proportion to the distance, so a
zoom out is a change of scale and nothing else: the screen spans the
same octaves of ground, which is what the window of levels is sized
for (environment/fog.rs). Nearer, they hold at their values here, so
a street-level view keeps its horizon.
Minimum-brightness floor shared by every lit surface — terrain and
placed cells, decor, actors — through the one shading source
(crates/pxl/web/render/src/frame/shader/shade.wgsl, `frame.floor`, carried
in the theme through state.rs). One shared constant, so terrain
and objects cannot dim apart. Tune this one number to retune every
surface's night floor at once.
Judged on a real device, not a desktop monitor — a darker floor that read
as convincing night on a monitor was simply too dark to see the world on
a phone screen.
Raising this alone flattens the scene, since it lifts every face by the
same amount and erases the shading that carries depth. It moves together
with the moon's directional light, which adds
brightness that still differs face to face.
Fresnel/rim highlight, applied uniformly to everything lit — terrain,
placed objects, decor and actors alike, since one shading source lights
them (crates/pxl/web/render/src/frame/shader/shade.wgsl) — a thin bright edge on
faces that graze the view direction, the classic "toy block catching
light at its silhouette" cue. Originally object-only (meant to help
placed objects read as distinct from terrain cells sharing the same
block palette), but a shared render pipeline shouldn't treat one
geometry role differently from another for the same shader term, so it
applies everywhere show_rim_light is on. The falloff's exponent is the
shader's; this is the linear scale on it, the one that controls peak
brightness, written into the frame uniform.
The canvas's resolution. The colour grade and the vignette are the
shaders' own constants (crates/pxl/web/render/src/frame/shader/{grade,shade}.wgsl);
the rest of the post stack three ran — contact AO, bloom, god rays,
SMAA — is at b9e31004 with its tuning.
The canvas draws at the device's pixel ratio clamped to this
(issue/20260911-taa-tried-and-closed.md on why the cap is where it is).
